title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly had a second affair with another Nvidia exec
summary: A new report says that video evidence of the affair exists, but was swept under the rug.
body: Days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy (China denies any espionage ), The New York Times has reported new claims that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him: Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia VP who oversees the company's healthcare tech-related efforts. NYT cites five sources who work at the company, and says that it is aware of, but has not seen, video evidence of the affair. It's a story you could see playing out in a film noir thriller. According to NYT's sources, Huang and Powell were seen "being affectionate" at a hotel in the vicinity of an Nvidia conference earlier this year. A bystander allegedly captured a video of the interaction, but according to the report was made an offer by security personnel—details unknown—in return for signing an NDA. Nvidia's board of directors is investigating the national security concerns raised by the affair Huang disclosed over the weekend, and The Wall Street Journal reported today that the board is preparing to oust the CEO. At the time of writing, the company has not commented on this new allegation. PC Gamer has reached out.

body: There was some fun conversation here at PC Gamer recently about the anachronistic name of The Golden Joystick Awards. Who even uses a joystick anymore? Flight sim diehards, fighting game enthusiasts, and not many others. So why is it called that? Joysticks , really? Simply put, the name reflects the age of the awards, which debuted in 1983, making it the longest-running publicly-voted videogame awards show of all time, according to Wikipedia. Back in those days, joysticks were it, and trust me, they weren't the sweet pieces of hardware we have access to now. But we loved 'em! And we used them to play games like the Golden Joysticks' first-ever game of the year, Jetpac. It was a banger! Here we are, 43 years later, and much has changed: From a tiny ceremony handing out five trophies, the Golden Joysticks have grown to become one of the biggest videogame awards events of the year, watched by millions of people around the world on just about every streaming platform you can name. body: The Steam Deck is the most popular handheld gaming PC, and no doubt a lot of you own one already. It's also far from the most powerful handheld on the market, meaning devs have to get optimisation just right to allow the Deck to maintain 60 or even 30 fps. Now, Valve is letting everyone see exactly how well those optimisations are made by listing average Steam Deck frame rate data on game store pages. Valve explains that this applies to any game that's been tested for Steam Deck compatibility, not just Verified ones. It applies to 'Verified', 'Playable', and 'Unsupported' ones. Apparently that means thousands of games right now. The data is based on what different users have opted in to provide, which, despite only being for opt-inners, presumably still gives a big sample size.
